title: Managua Airport (MGA) to Granada
origin: Managua Augusto C. Sandino International Airport (MGA)
duration: 45–60 min by car outside rush hour
summary: Granada is the most common first stop after landing in Managua. There is no direct public bus from the airport: you either pre-book a transfer, take an airport taxi, rent a car at the arrivals hall, or ride into Managua first and catch a bus from a city terminal.

options.cost: Roughly US$50–90 per vehicle (2026 operator pricing)
options.detail: Door to door, driver waits in arrivals with your name. The safest option for late-night landings and the one most travelers pick with luggage.

options.cost: Around US$40 per car, agreed before leaving
options.detail: Licensed taxis wait outside arrivals. Agree the fare in US dollars or córdobas before getting in; meters are not used.

options.cost: From about US$24 per day plus deposit (comparison pricing at MGA)
options.duration: About 45–60 min drive on the Masaya highway
options.detail: Rental desks are in the arrivals hall. Minimum age 21 with a young-driver fee under 25; a credit card deposit is charged at pick-up. Makes sense if Granada is the first of several stops.

options.cost: About US$2 in fares
options.detail: Taxi to a Managua terminal (UCA or Huembes), then a Granada bus. Cheapest by far, but slow with luggage and not advisable after dark.

recommended: Pre-book a private transfer if you land after 6 p.m. or travel with more than one bag. Rent at the airport only if you will keep the car for the rest of the trip.
caution: Transfer and taxi prices are set by operators and move with fuel costs and season; the figures here were checked in September 2026. Managua traffic can add 30 minutes on weekday evenings.

title: Managua Airport (MGA) to León
origin: Managua Augusto C. Sandino International Airport (MGA)
summary: León sits north-west of Managua on the road to the Pacific volcanoes. A private transfer is the only option that goes straight from the terminal; shared shuttles run on fixed afternoon departures and public buses leave from Managua's terminals, not the airport.

options.cost: About US$80 for 1–3 people, US$140 for a van (operator pricing)
options.detail: Booked through hostels, hotels or tour marketplaces. Door to door and the only choice that works for night arrivals.

options.cost: About US$25 per person
options.detail: One published departure in the early afternoon (13:00, arriving around 16:00). Cheaper than a private car for solo travelers, but you wait for the fixed time.

options.cost: From about US$24 per day plus deposit
options.detail: Pick up in arrivals and follow the Carretera Nueva a León. Good if León is your base for volcano and beach day trips.

options.cost: About US$9–10 total including the taxi to the terminal
options.duration: Close to 4 h door to door
options.detail: Taxi to the UCA terminal, then a León-bound bus. Fine in daylight with light luggage.

recommended: Solo daytime arrivals: shared shuttle. Groups or evening flights: private transfer. Multi-stop trips: rental car.
caution: Shuttle departure times and prices are published by individual operators and change by season. The 2 h estimate assumes light traffic leaving Managua.

title: Managua Airport (MGA) to San Juan del Sur
origin: Managua Augusto C. Sandino International Airport (MGA)
distance: South along the Pan-American Highway through Rivas
summary: San Juan del Sur is the beach town most international visitors head to, and the airport-to-beach run is the single most booked transfer in the country. Private shuttles are expensive per vehicle but cheap per seat when you fill them; public buses exist but leave from Managua, not the airport.

options.cost: About US$140–170 per vehicle
options.detail: Operators run daily roughly 07:30–19:30. Split among a group it is the fastest and simplest option; ask the driver to stop at a supermarket in Rivas if you are self-catering.

options.cost: From about US$40 per person
options.detail: Seat-by-seat vans that consolidate travelers on fixed departures. Book ahead; they fill on weekends and holidays.

options.cost: From about US$24 per day plus deposit
options.detail: The road is paved and straightforward: Pan-American Highway south to Rivas, then the branch to San Juan del Sur. Useful for reaching the surf beaches north and south of town, which have no public transport.

options.cost: About US$3 in bus fares plus the taxi to the terminal
options.detail: Taxi to the Huembes terminal, then a direct bus (a few departures a day) or any Rivas bus and a connection. Daylight only.

recommended: Groups: private shuttle. Solo or couples on a budget: shared shuttle. Surfers who want the outer beaches: rental car.
caution: Per-vehicle prices vary widely between operators and by pick-up time; night surcharges are common. The figures were checked in September 2026 and are indicative, not a tariff.

title: San Jorge (Rivas) to Ometepe Island by ferry
distance: Lake crossing from San Jorge to Moyogalpa
summary: Every visitor to Ometepe crosses Lake Nicaragua from the San Jorge pier, a short taxi ride from Rivas. Car ferries and smaller lanchas alternate through the day; foot passengers just turn up, while vehicles must be reserved.

options.cost: About C$50 (roughly US$1.50) per person each way; children under 5 free
options.detail: Departures run from about 07:00 to 17:30 daily in both directions. Ferries are steadier than lanchas when the lake is choppy; if you get seasick, wait for a ferry.

options.cost: Vehicle fare charged at the port on top of passenger tickets
options.detail: Anything larger than a motorcycle needs a reserved space. Arrive about an hour early for registration and port fees. Most rental contracts allow the crossing, but confirm in writing.

options.cost: Taxi from Rivas, San Juan del Sur or Granada
options.duration: 15 min from Rivas; about 45 min from San Juan del Sur
options.detail: Buses from Managua and Granada stop in Rivas, not at the pier. Shared shuttles from San Juan del Sur or Granada usually include the pier drop-off.

recommended: Take any morning departure and keep the last afternoon boat as a buffer, not a plan. Reserve vehicle space the day before.
caution: Timetables are seasonal, weather-dependent and different on Sundays and national holidays; strong winds cancel lanchas first. Confirm the day's schedule at the pier or with the operator by phone.

title: Managua to San José (Costa Rica) by bus via Peñas Blancas
distance: Pan-American Highway south through Rivas to the Peñas Blancas border, then on to San José
summary: The international bus lines are the simplest way to cross into Costa Rica: the bus waits while you clear both immigration posts at Peñas Blancas, the busiest land border in the country. Budget the exit and entry fees in US dollars cash.

options.mode: International bus (Tica Bus and similar lines)
options.cost: About US$30–35 per person depending on seat class
options.detail: Daily departures from the Managua terminal two blocks above the old Cine Dorado in Barrio Bolonia; the same lines also pick up in Granada and Rivas. Book a day or two ahead in high season.

options.mode: Costa Rica land exit tax (leaving Costa Rica northbound)
options.cost: US$8 per person
options.duration: Minutes at a Banco de Costa Rica kiosk or online beforehand
options.detail: Only applies when you leave Costa Rica by land. Pay at the BCR kiosk at the border or online before travel and keep the receipt for immigration.

options.cost: US$10 per person, cash
options.detail: Charged to every foreign visitor except citizens of the CA-4 countries (Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua). Travelers also report a small municipal or immigration fee of a few dollars at Peñas Blancas; carry small US bills.

options.mode: Shuttle or private car to the border, then onward transport
options.cost: Varies by operator; more expensive than the bus
options.duration: Shorter waits than a full bus, but the same immigration steps
options.detail: Popular from San Juan del Sur to Liberia or the Guanacaste beaches. Rental cars normally cannot be taken across the border; plan a car swap.

recommended: Take the international bus from Managua or Granada and carry at least US$20 per person in small bills for the fees. Passports need six months' validity.
caution: Bus fares come from booking aggregators and change with class and season. Fees are as published by each government in 2026; extra municipal charges reported by travelers are not on official tariffs, so treat them as possible, not certain.

title: Managua to Big Corn and Little Corn Island
origin: Managua Augusto C. Sandino International Airport (MGA)
distance: Domestic flight to Big Corn (RNI), then a 30-minute panga to Little Corn
duration: About 1 h 15 min flying plus 20–30 min by boat
summary: The Caribbean Corn Islands are reached by La Costeña's daily domestic flights from Managua; Little Corn has no airstrip, so you finish with a small open boat (panga) from Big Corn. Flights and pangas run on fixed times, so the whole day is a chain of connections.

options.mode: La Costeña flight, Managua to Big Corn Island
options.cost: Around US$95 one way, about US$190 return (2026 reported fares)
options.detail: Daily service, typically two departures a day (morning and early afternoon). Check in at the domestic terminal at least 1.5 h before departure; small aircraft with strict baggage weight limits.

options.mode: Panga, Big Corn to Little Corn
options.cost: US$10 per person, cash
options.detail: Published high-season departures are about 10:00 and 16:30 from Big Corn and 06:30 and 13:30 from Little Corn; in low season operators have run a single daily boat each way. Take a taxi from the airstrip to the municipal dock.

options.cost: A few dollars, flat island fare
options.detail: Taxis meet every flight. If your panga time is tight, go straight to the dock and buy food later on Little Corn.

recommended: Book the morning flight so you make the mid-day panga and are not stranded on Big Corn overnight. Keep return flights at least a day before any international connection.
caution: Bad weather suspends pangas and can delay flights; the schedule is a chain, so build in slack. Flight times and fares change by season and were checked in September 2026 against the airline's site and recent traveler reports.
